context: Decide the reconciliation: either (a) narrow the contract so permanence attaches at publication rather than at commit, which matches reality today and makes #1537 legal, or (b) keep commit-time minting and add an alias/redirect table the Explorer consumes, seeded from path-privacy-migration.manifest.json which already records every old-to-new pair. Also correct the documented format to include the sha8 suffix. Record as an ADR either way, and do it before the Explorer first deploys.
description: Codex P1 on PR #1537. docs/reference/hosted-results-contract.md defines public_result_id with Stability 'Permanent once minted. Never reused for a different result.' and Minting 'Phase 1: on commit to results-data/'. By that definition IDs mint on commit, and #1537 re-derives all 207. The Explorer pipeline has no consumer for path-privacy-migration.manifest.json and publishes no aliases or redirects, so any ID change is unrecoverable for an external link. Assessment: no PRACTICAL breakage today - the Explorer has never deployed (docs.yml has only ever run on pull_request events, origin/release carries zero bundles), so no /results/r/<id> URL has ever resolved publicly and nothing can be bookmarked. But the contract's own minting definition is commit-time, and the corpus is now public on published-results, so the letter of the contract is violated even though no consumer exists. The two must be reconciled BEFORE any public launch, because after launch the same re-derivation becomes impossible without a redirect map. Note the documented format in that table also omits the -{sha8} suffix the implementation actually appends, so the contract already diverges from the code.

preserves.behavior: Whatever is decided must hold before the Explorer's first public deploy
